assessment: The engine is fed; the mana and the payoff surface are not. Four of the six bench cards make the ten and six pool cards join them: the mana package (Cabal Coffers, Urborg, Crypt Ghast, Culling the Weak) attacks the 43.5% fast-mana figure and the 60.6% engine-mana figure directly, while Pawn of Ulamog, Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric, Bontu's Monument and Drivnod buy bodies and pod-wide conversion. Mikaeus carries seven of eleven infinites, and the answer is NOT to buy more Mikaeus dependents — Plague Belcher, Walking Ballista, Triskelion and Altar of Dementia all fail that test and none is here. Pawn of Ulamog and Drivnod each complete five to seven lines that never name him, Exquisite Blood goes from one partner to three, and Imp's Mischief covers the targeted-removal case. Two bench cards stayed in the box; two of the ten (Urborg, Culling the Weak) are already in the share files and cost nothing.

ten.why: The deck runs 22 Swamps, so Coffers taps for more black than the rest of the manabase combined by turn 5, and it costs a land slot rather than a spell slot — that is the cheapest possible answer to engine mana sitting at 60.6% unassisted by turn 10 (goldfish_metrics.json, 10,000 iterations, seed 42).
ten.when: Buy it first. It is the only card here that fixes mana without competing with the engine for a turn: it comes down on a land drop and turns on the same turn Yawgmoth does.

bench_verdicts.why: Grave Pact is already sleeved and this is the same effect one mana dearer; Drivnod, Carnage Dominus costs the same five and makes that Grave Pact fire twice per death while also doubling four drains, so the slot is spent better.

Seven mana on a deck whose commander lands turn 4 and whose kills mean-assemble on turns 5.5 to 6.7 — a card you cast after the game has been decided is not a card. Everything it does (reanimation, edicts, a body) is already in the 99 at three to five mana.

gaps: Ophiomancer is NOT on this list, and the reason is a tribal line the indexes cannot see. Its ability is 'At the beginning of each upkeep, IF YOU CONTROL NO SNAKES, create a 1/1 black Snake creature token with deathtouch' — and South Wind Avatar is a Creature — Snake Spirit Avatar in the maindeck, the only Snake in the 100. While the Avatar is on the battlefield Ophiomancer makes nothing at all, so it is blank on exactly the board you most want: the Avatar is the sole partner for Exquisite Blood, the third named kill at 32.5% tutor-assisted by turn 10, a pod-wide lifegain payoff, and the 4-toughness counter sink stack 005 (pass) measured at exactly +4 activations. Cutting the Avatar to make Ophiomancer live would trade a verified, load-bearing card for a conditional one and orphan a checker-passed stack; the fodder slot goes to Bontu's Monument instead, which no card in the 99 can switch off.

Not one line on this list is verified. Exquisite Blood + Marauding Blight-Priest and Exquisite Blood + Starscape Cleric are recorded infinite in combo_details.json (bracket 3, popularity 50,637 and 21,354) and both need a resolve-stack run before anyone prints them as kills — particularly whether the mandatory loop terminates only under state-based actions in a four-player pod.

The obsolescence index lists Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER // Sephiroth, One-Winged Angel as a strictly-better replacement for BOTH Ayara, First of Locthwain and Mirkwood Bats. Reading the cards refutes that here: Sephiroth's drain is single-target, and stack 004 measured a single-target drain at a 3.5x penalty against the each-opponent class, while stack 008 measured Bats at 13 triggers / 52 pod life. The index is format-agnostic and does not know which side of the trigger this deck is paid on. That is why Sephiroth is not in the ten.

Mirkwood Bats is not uniformly a creation-side payoff and no pick here should be priced as if it were: stack 008 (pass) measured 13 triggers on the Yawgmoth line, stack 007 (pass) measured 2 on the Blowfly line and found Bats HALTS that loop, because its 2/3 body survives the forced counter. Starscape Cleric's Offspring token is a one-time creation event, not a loop claim; anything stronger needs its own scenario.

Whether Drivnod doubles Mirkwood Bats is unsettled and should not be assumed. Bats triggers on 'you create or sacrifice a token'; Drivnod's replacement is worded around 'a creature dying'. A sacrifice causes a death, but the trigger condition is the sacrifice — that distinction decides the answer and only a stack scenario settles it.

Pawn of Ulamog's clause is 'another NONTOKEN creature you control dies', so its own Eldrazi Spawn do not feed it. Every one of its seven lines therefore leans on a recursive nontoken body (Reassembling Skeleton) rather than on token fodder; none is verified.

The goldfish 'fast mana' target's any_of is Sol Ring, Ancient Tomb and Dark Ritual only. Culling the Weak, Cabal Coffers and Crypt Ghast are not in it, so their effect on the 43.5% figure is unmeasured — widening that target is a goldfish_targets.json edit and a re-run, not a claim this analysis can make.

As cut, the ten drops four lands (Survivors' Encampment, Archway Commons, Path of Ancestry, Gemstone Mine) and adds two (Cabal Coffers, Urborg), taking the list from 38 land entries to 36 while adding Crypt Ghast and Culling the Weak as mana. Every natural_cut here is a suggestion; mana-analysis and goldfish both need re-running before any of these rates are quoted again.
